title: The Price of Living Near Sodom

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The four kings seized all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food; then they went away. They also carried off Abram's nephew Lot and his possessions, since he was living in Sodom. - Gen 14:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the bill coming due. Lot is carried off as a prisoner of war, and Scripture tells us exactly why: "since he was living in Sodom." Notice the quiet progression. In chapter 13 he pitched his tents near Sodom. Now he is living in Sodom. The drift continued, as drift always does.

And now Sodom's troubles are Lot's troubles. When judgement fell on the city, it fell on him too. He hadn't chosen Sodom's sin, but he had chosen Sodom's address - and you cannot separate the two. Where we live shapes what happens to us.

This is the sobering truth about compromise: we share the fate of what we attach ourselves to. Lot wanted the benefits of the plain without its consequences. It doesn't work that way. The city he moved toward for prosperity is the city that cost him everything.

Scripture warns God's people about entanglement precisely because it loves us: "Do not be yoked together with unbelievers" (2 Cor 6:14) - not because others are worthless, but because attachment brings shared consequences. Ask yourself honestly what you have moved toward for its advantages. When trouble comes to it, trouble comes to you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What have you attached yourself to whose consequences you'll share?
- Has a gradual drift put you somewhere you never intended to be?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, show me where drift has carried me somewhere I never meant to go. Give me courage to move, before what I've attached myself to costs me what I cannot afford to lose.
Amen.
